# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## Working Principles (user-mandated, 最高优先级)

用户时间与预算有限，**每个任务都必须为省时间/省 token 服务**：

- **最短路径**：只为当前任务做最小必要改动；不顺手重构、不新增无关文件、不写长篇注释或文档。
- **省 token 的读法**：先用 grep/glob 定位，再带 offset/limit 定点读；禁止重复整文件读取或整文件回显；改动优先用 edit，不要重写大文件。
- **少开 agent**：默认由 Lead 单独完成。只有当任务可拆成互不依赖的大块、且并行确实更快时才用 teammates；subagent 的上下文同样是成本。
- **验证从简**：本项目无测试套件，只做必要的最小验证（如 GDScript 语法/加载检查），不跑完整试玩流程，除非任务明确要求。
- **输出精简**：结论先行，只列改动点与验证结果，不复述代码。
- **任务完成必须弹 Windows 通知**：每次交付结束前执行
  `pwsh -NoProfile -File scripts\dev\notify.ps1 -Title "HonorKing · <任务名>" -Message "<一句话结果>"`
  （脚本已就绪，失败会静默降级，不阻断交付）。

## Project Overview

HonorKing — a 3D MOBA game built with **Godot 4.5** (Forward Plus renderer). All game logic is written in **GDScript**. The game simulates a 5v5 Honor of Kings-style match: one player-controlled hero plus 4 AI teammates versus 5 AI enemies across a three-lane map with jungle, turrets, and epic monsters.

## Development Commands

- **Run the game**: Open `project.godot` in the Godot 4.5 editor and press F5, or run `godot --path .` from the project root.
- **No tests, no build step**: There is no test suite or CI. The only way to verify changes is to run the game in the Godot editor.

## Architecture

### Autoloads (Globals)

Defined in `project.godot` → `[autoload]`. These singletons are available everywhere without `load()`:

| Autoload | Path | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `Config` | `scripts/core/Config.gd` | Constants: `MAP_SIZE=120`, `Team` enum (`PLAYER=0, ENEMY=1, NEUTRAL=2`) |
| `ItemDatabase` | `assets/ItemDatabase.gd` | All item definitions, synthesis trees, recommended build paths, `get_item()`, `can_build()`, `get_synthesis_cost()` |
| `SkillDatabase` | `assets/SkillDataBase.gd` | All skill definitions (hero skills + summoner spells), `get_skill()` |
| `GameManager` | `scripts/core/GameManager.gd` | Stub — currently empty (`_ready` and `_process` are no-ops) |
| `UiManager` | `scripts/ui/UI_Manager.gd` | Comprehensive UI: skill icons, shop, kill feed, hero detail panel (C key), target info, death recap, buff panel, damage/gold/heal popups |
| `CollisionSystem` | `scripts/core/CollisionSystem.gd` | Per-frame entity pushback to prevent overlapping (heroes ← → turrets, minions ← → turrets excluded) |

### Core Scripts (`scripts/core/`)

- **`BattleManager.gd`** — The central game controller (`class_name BattleManager`). Handles:
  - Map creation (ground planes, lane planes, river, high-ground circles)
  - Hero select UI → game start flow
  - Player hero + AI hero creation (one of each role: assassin/mage/marksman/warrior/support)
  - Turret, jungle camp, wall/bush placement
  - Minion wave spawning (3 lanes × 2 teams, with growth tables, siege/super/dragon minion variants)
  - Epic monster timers (Tyrant at 4min, Dragon at 4min)
  - Economy systems: kill/assist gold, tower gold, lane gold sharing, natural gold/exp, jungle item rules, support item rules
  - Input handling: left-click attack order, right-click move, raycasting for ground/target selection
  - Camera: follows player hero, minimap drag/jump override
  - Win condition: crystal destruction → game-over screen
  - Hero configs: `hero_configs` dictionary with base stats for all 17 heroes

- **`EntityDatabase.gd`** — Stub (empty `_ready`/`_process`).

- **`CameraController.gd`** — Standalone camera script (attached to a Camera3D), follows a `@export var target`. Currently unused — BattleManager controls the camera directly.

- **`MapGenerator.gd`** — Alternative map generator (creates a simpler 60×60 grass + river). Not used in the main game; BattleManager has its own `_create_map()`.

- **`CollisionSystem.gd`** — See Autoloads above.

### Entity Hierarchy (`scripts/entities/`)

All entities inherit from **`GameEntity`** (`class_name GameEntity extends CharacterBody3D`):

```
GameEntity
├── Hero (player & AI champions)
├── Turret (defensive structures)
├── Minion (lane creeps)
├── JungleMonster (neutral camps + epic monsters)
├── Bullet (projectile for ranged attacks and skill shots)
├── LinearBullet (directional projectile variant)
├── Wall (terrain obstacle)
├── Bush (stealth zone)
├── HealthPack (regen pickup)
├── TeleportZone (teleport pad)
└── prw (unidentified entity)
```

**`GameEntity`** provides:
- Base stats: `health`, `max_health`, `attack`, `armor`, `magic_resist`, `move_speed`, `attack_range`, `attack_speed`, `body_radius`, `level`
- State effects: slow, stun, knockup, freeze, suppress, silence, grievous wounds
- Shield system (`shield_remaining`/`shield_timer`)
- Marker system for stacking passives (e.g., Zhen Ji freeze, Angela burn, Marco Polo stacks)
- Damage calculation: `take_damage()` with armor/MR reduction formula (`resistance / (resistance + 602)`), penetration, crit detection
- Hunt DoT system (jungle item burn)
- Lifesteal application (physical and magical, with grievous wounds reduction)
- Death handling: `die(killer)` → signals, gold/exp distribution, buff transfer
- Kill assist detection (nearest enemy hero within 12 units)

**`Hero`** (`scripts/entities/Hero.gd`, ~2150 lines) — The largest and most complex class:
- **Stats**: base stats + role-based growth per level (tank/warrior/assassin/marksman/mage/support)
- **Equipment**: 6-slot inventory, `buy_equipment()` with component synthesis, `_apply_equipment_bonuses()` recalculates all stats from items, 100+ unique item passive/active effects
- **Skills**: 3 hero skills + summoner spell + recover, each with cooldowns, mana costs, charge/restore system, upgrade via Ctrl+key or auto-level
- **Hero-specific logic**: Each hero has hardcoded special behavior in `_physics_process()` (Arthur passive heal + W shield rotation, Donghuang orbs, Li Bai sword auras, Zhang Fei transformation + mana, Lanling stealth, Taiyi Q channeling)
- **Combat**: auto-attack with bullet spawning (ranged) or instant (melee), crit, on-hit effects from 20+ items
- **Input**: WASD movement, right-click move orders, left-click attack orders, skill hotkeys 1-3, summoner spell key, item actives (keys 6-0, V, =, -)
- **Post-game stats**: `damage_dealt_to_heroes`, `damage_taken_from_heroes`, `healing_done`, `cc_duration_dealt`, `turret_damage`, `jungle_gold`, `last_hits`, `gold_history`

**Other entity notes**:
- `Bullet.gd` / `LinearBullet.gd` — Projectiles with speed, damage, pierce, slow, red buff burn, team affiliation
- `Turret.gd` — Auto-attacks nearby enemies, has outer/inner/high/crystal tiers with different stats
- `Minion.gd` — Follows waypoints along lanes, attacks enemies in range
- `JungleMonster.gd` — Has `activity_radius` (leash range), `buff_type` for red/blue buff
- `Wall.gd` / `Bush.gd` — Static collision/stealth volumes
- `HeroAI.gd` — AI controller for bot heroes (attached as child of Hero)

### Asset Scripts (`assets/`)

- **`ItemDatabase.gd`** — Massive dictionary of all equipment items with: name, tier (1-4), cost, stat bonuses, `requires` (synthesis components), `passive`/`active` descriptions, category tags. Key functions: `get_item(id)`, `can_build(id, owned)`, `get_synthesis_cost()`, `get_synthesis_tree()`, `get_recommended_items(role)`.
- **`SkillDataBase.gd`** — Dictionary of all skills (hero abilities + summoner spells). Each skill defines: `type` (0=targeted, 1=AoE, 3=linear, 4=dash, 6=shield), `cooldown`, `mana_cost`, `cast_range`, `damage`, `radius`, `duration`, etc.
- **`Skill.gd`** — Skill resource class (`class_name Skill extends Resource`). Properties: `skill_name`, `type`, `cooldown`, `cd_bonus`, `mana_cost`, `power_bonus`, `cast_range`, `cast_time`, `damage`, `radius`, `duration`, `self_displacement`, `shield_amount`, `is_channeling`, `charge`, `restore`, `restore_bonus`.

### UI System (`scripts/ui/`)

**`UI_Manager.gd`** (~1600 lines) handles all in-game UI:
- Skill bar with 8 icon slots (4 skills + summoner + 2 active equipment)
- Shop system (O key): categorized grid (物理/法术/防御/靴子/打野/游走/保命), detail panel, buy/sell, component synthesis display
- Recommended equipment (B key to quick-buy)
- Kill feed (multi-kill announcements, tower/epic monster kills)
- Hero detail panel (C key): team stats, all hero cards with stats/skills/equipment/KDA
- Death recap (auto-shows on death): damage source breakdown with stacked bar charts
- Target detail panel (shows selected target's stats)
- Buff/debuff display panel
- Damage/heal/gold floating numbers (world-space → screen projection)
- Respawn widgets (hero icons with HP rings and respawn timers)

Internal classes: `SkillIcon` (draws cooldown overlay, upgrade indicator), `RespawnWidget` (HP ring + death timer), `DamageChart`.

### Key Mechanics to Understand

1. **Damage formula**: `actual_damage = raw_damage × (1 - resistance / (resistance + 602))` where resistance already accounts for flat and percentage penetration.
2. **Attack speed**: Uses a threshold table (Model A from Honor of Kings) — panel AS% maps to discrete attack interval tiers.
3. **Economy sharing**: Multiple heroes near a minion kill split gold (100%/80%/55%/43%/37% for 1-5 players). Jungle/support items modify this.
4. **Minion growth**: Minion stats interpolate from growth tables at `game_time / 60` minutes, with melee/ranged/siege/super/dragon variants.
5. **Item synthesis**: Buying a high-tier item that requires owned components only costs the difference. Selling refunds 70%.
6. **Buff system**: Active buffs are stored as dictionaries with timers, processed each frame in `_calculate_buff()`. Red/blue buffs transfer on kill.
7. **Hero-specific code**: Each hero has unique mechanics hardcoded with `if display_name == "..."` checks in `_physics_process()`, `_perform_attack()`, and `_finish_casting()`. Adding a new hero requires touching Hero.gd in multiple places plus adding skill definitions to SkillDatabase.

### Assets Not Tracked in Scripts

- `icon.svg` — Game icon
- `.godot/` — Engine cache (shader cache, editor state, import files)
- `scenes/battle.tscn` — The single main scene (binary .tscn format)
- 3D models, textures, and audio are created programmatically (PlaneMesh, CapsuleMesh, TorusMesh, StandardMaterial3D) — there are no imported art assets.

tools.description: Execute a PowerShell command (`pwsh -Command`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh pwsh process; pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Paths use native Windows form (`C:\...`); read environment variables with `$env:NAME`. Managed `$env:DSH_*` variables expose current harness environment facts. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. On Windows a force-killed command settles as `[exit code: 1]` without a signal marker — treat it as an interruption, not a command failure. Provide `description` before `command` in the arguments. Before any delete or move, verify that the resolved absolute target path is the intended one; never run it against a computed path you have not checked. Do not assign to automatic variables such as `$HOME`; variable names are case-insensitive, so `$home` is the same read-only variable. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]`, a policy denial: do not retry another way. Under the Windows sandbox, read-only pwsh runs in PowerShell ConstrainedLanguage mode, while workspace-write stays in FullLanguage unless host policy says otherwise. In read-only, prefer cmdlets and core types (`[string]`, `[datetime]`, `[regex]`, `[guid]`); .NET static calls (`[System.IO.*]::`, `[math]::`), `Add-Type`, COM objects, and reflection fail with "only core types" errors. `-f` formatting, property access, and core cmdlets work. In both confined modes, programs cannot open named pipes, so a command that captures another program's output through piped stdio (Node.js `child_process.spawn`/`exec` with the default `stdio: 'pipe'`) fails with EPERM, while `stdio: 'inherit'` and `stdio: 'ignore'` spawns work and PowerShell's own pipelines are unaffected. Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. A stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) end the whole script instead of producing `null`. The script has no filesystem, network, timer, or Node.js APIs; the agents do the work.

224: # 最深一层缺失的素材件（主机 _find_missing_basic 镜像）
225: func _missing_basic(target_id: String) -> String:
226: 	var target := ItemDatabase.get_item(target_id)
227: 	if target.is_empty() or not target.has("requires"):
228: 		return target_id
229: 	for req_id: String in target.get("requires", []):
230: 		var need := 0
231: 		for r in target["requires"]:
232: 			if str(r) == req_id:
233: 				need += 1
234: 		if _owned_n(req_id) < need:
235: 			return _missing_basic(req_id)
236: 	return target_id

238: # 下一件（推荐买的第一个：素材齐→合成大件；否则→最底层素材；槽满→补差价合成/升级已有件）
239: func _plan_next(plan: Array) -> String:
240: 	if _equip.size() >= 6:
241: 		# 1. 推荐列表里能补差价合成的（至少持有一件素材）
242: 		for id in plan:
243: 			if _owned_n(id) > 0:
244: 				continue
245: 			for req_id: String in ItemDatabase.get_item(id).get("requires", []):
246: 				if _owned_n(req_id) > 0:
247: 					return id
248: 		# 2. 升级已有低级装（2 阶→合大件 / 1 阶→先合中阶）
249: 		for owned_id in _equip:
250: 			var ot := int(ItemDatabase.get_item(str(owned_id)).get("tier", 1))
251: 			if ot >= 3:
252: 				continue
253: 			if ot == 2:
254: 				for rid in plan:
255: 					if _owned_n(rid) > 0:
256: 						continue
257: 					if str(owned_id) in ItemDatabase.get_item(rid).get("requires", []):
258: 						return rid
259: 			else:
260: 				for rid in plan:
261: 					if _owned_n(rid) > 0:
262: 						continue
263: 					for mid_id: String in ItemDatabase.get_item(rid).get("requires", []):
264: 						if _owned_n(mid_id) > 0:
265: 							continue
266: 						if str(owned_id) in ItemDatabase.get_item(mid_id).get("requires", []):
267: 							return mid_id
268: 		# 3. 兜底第一个未拥有
269: 		for id in plan:
270: 			if _owned_n(id) == 0:
271: 				return id
272: 		return str(plan[0]) if not plan.is_empty() else ""
273: 	# 未满槽：素材齐→合成大件；否则最底层缺失件
274: 	for id in plan:
275: 		if _owned_n(id) > 0:
276: 			continue
277: 		if ItemDatabase.can_build(id, _equip):
278: 			return id
279: 	for id in plan:
280: 		if _owned_n(id) > 0:
281: 			continue
282: 		var miss := _missing_basic(id)
283: 		if miss != "":
284: 			return miss
285: 	return ""

287: # 现在补多少钱能到手（总价 - 已拥有素材折价）
288: func _need_cost(id: String) -> int:
289: 	var it := ItemDatabase.get_item(id)
290: 	if it.is_empty():
291: 		return 0
292: 	var cost := int(it.get("cost", 0))
293: 	for req_id: String in it.get("requires", []):
294: 		var need := 0
295: 		for r in it["requires"]:
296: 			if str(r) == req_id:
297: 				need += 1
298: 		var own := mini(_owned_n(req_id), need)
299: 		if own > 0:
300: 			cost -= own * int(ItemDatabase.get_item(req_id).get("cost", 0))
301: 	return maxi(cost, 0)

I could add mouse wheel handling in _gui_input to adjust _scroll (safe improvement, but task doesn't demand; alignment includes scroll behavior maybe). I'll add InputEventMouseButton wheel handling to scroll — harmless and makes _scroll meaningful. But careful: parent might handle? It's fine.

  Item cards: 2 columns, width = (1080 - 8.1)/2 ≈ 535.95, height 76 (host min height 76; rows exactly 76? GridContainer v_sep 5.4 and button min height 76 → row height 76). Net doesn't have selected item state; clicking an item currently buys/sells directly. Host: clicking card selects it and shows detail; buy via button. To align, change interaction: click item card → select (show detail); click 购买 button in detail → buy; click 出售 button → sell; owned strip buttons → select item. That satisfies "推荐装备与出装路线区" being present and aligned in styling.

Now I have host shop fully. Important: host item list per category is explicit ID lists (not class mapping). Net uses class mapping; this causes different item sets. Should align category contents too! Use the host `_shop_categories()` ID lists verbatim in NetShopPanel — that's client-side ItemDatabase-only, no host runtime data. That's a strong alignment win. The list includes "辅助" mapped to roam; we're using 7 tabs, so use the same lists for 7 categories; 游走 uses roam. The "保命" list in host is ["blood_rage"...]. Using explicit lists makes ordering determined by host sort: tier desc, then cost desc. Net currently sorts by rank ascending (tier*cost). Host sorts tier desc, cost desc. Align.

Let me verify those item IDs all exist in ItemDatabase (else skipped anyway with get_item empty check).

Now check the feed path: _rec is set, and _hero_name. HeroPickData.HERO_ROLE used in _plan. host get_recommended_items(hero.role). Client has HeroPickData? It's used in current file; exists presumably. Keep.

Now design the new NetShopPanel draw.

Key design decision: 2-column cards + detail pane. Let me check whether the user's expectation "物品格 6 列" means they want 6 columns preserved. Hmm. If I switch to 2 columns, a user looking at it might say "you changed the layout entirely, this isn't what I asked" — but if it now matches single-player, that's the goal. The complaint is "联机版和单机版的商店面板不太一样" → make net look like host. Host has 2 columns. So 2 columns is correct. The prompt's "6 列" is likely the Lead describing the current net layout (which they know) and saying to align its row height/column width/gap with host... Host has no 6 cols. So the Lead's spec is imprecise; task-1 itself says "以主机 API 实际渲染结果为准".

I'll implement host replica: 2-col grid + right detail + bottom owned strip + recommendation compact line. Keep direct-click buy semantics? Host card click = select; buy button in detail. Since alignment includes "购买/出售按钮", implement select + detail purchase. But mobile users might be used to direct click purchase; host requires selecting then buying. Replicating host is the task.

Hmm, but maintain "点击格子购买/出售" behavior compatibility? Task requirement 2 says "_gui_input/_unhandled_input 行为兼容" (behavior compatible) — this is notable! It says keep behavior compatible: clicking a cell buys/sells. Hmm, "保持现有公开 API 不变... 方法 ... _gui_input/_unhandled_input 行为兼容". Behavior compatible maybe means O/B/Esc keys, click close, click purchase/sell still work. Selecting-then-buying is a change but arguably still "compatible" (you can still buy by clicking). To be safe and user-friendly, I can support BOTH: first click on card selects it and shows detail; second click on an already-selected card buys it (or if owned, opens sell). Plus explicit 购买/出售 buttons in detail pane. Hmm, direct buy on first click is risky (accidental purchase). Host behavior = select only. But original net = buy directly. Which is "compatible"? Keep direct click = buy/sell (preserves behavior), and add detail buttons too; card click also selects. That's most compatible and gives host-like detail UI. I'll do: click card → select AND execute original action (buy if affordable/not owned, sell if owned)? Then detail pane 购买/出售 buttons are redundant but host-like. Double action may surprise. Alternative: card click only selects; detail buttons buy/sell. The task says align hit zones with new layout, not preserve exact semantics. Hmm.

I think the cleanest: click card → select (show details). Detail pane has 购买 / 出售 buttons (host replicas). Owned strip buttons → select owned item (host behavior). B quick buy unaffected. But original net users could no longer one-tap buy; they'd tap card then buy button = 2 taps, same as host. This is "align". Risk of Lead complaining "clicking item no longer buys". But task acceptance focuses on visual alignment. I'll do card click = select, and also make double-click? No.

Hmm, wait. There's a subtlety: If card click only selects, then user needs to notice the detail pane button. Fine, host does that.

Alternatively keep card click = select + buy in one, while detail shows info/sell. I lean to host behavior.

Let me now also check NetRosterPanel for how it structures "选中项 + 详情" style maybe. Not necessary.

Let me define geometry precisely relative to panel (drawer):
- PANEL_W = 2000 (constant, actual host px at 2400 canvas). But viewport may be wider than 2400 (e.g. 2560x1400); host drawer still 2000 wide centered. Panel x = (area.x - 2000)/2, y=0, h=area.y (host drawer anchors full height; virtual height is 1400 but visible rect height may be > or < ? Project stretch canvas_items expand: virtual height fixed 1400, virtual width = aspect*1400. get_visible_rect().size in a Control is in canvas coordinates → width = actual virtual width (>=2400), height 1400 constant. Wait is that right? In host, ui_scale uses vp width/2400, comment "横屏下虚拟高度恒为 1400、宽度随设备变化（≥2400）". So visible rect height = 1400 always, width varies. But NetShopPanel currently uses area for dim and centers panel horizontally, with PANEL_H fixed 1250. OK so use rect: x=(area.x-2000)/2, y=0, w=2000, h=1400 (area.y). Host drawer height = visible height = 1400.

But hold on: if visible rect width is e.g. 3000, host drawer is still 2000 wide centered. ui_scale = 3000/2400*1.35 = 1.6875, so fonts bigger but drawer same 2000. Replicate exactly: panel 2000 wide centered.

Host rs = ui_scale() in actual px. So _us() = maxf(1.0, area.x/2400)*1.35.

Now all host dimensions that were multiplied by rs:
- title pos 20*rs, 10; font 20*rs; gold.
- close font 26*rs; close button 50x50 at right-56..-6, y 6..56 (offset matters relative to drawer, no rs multiplication! close offsets are raw pixels, size 50x50).
- tabs: container at 20*rs,45; separation 6*rs; button 96*rs x 42*rs; font 14*rs.
- grid scroll offsets: top 110, bottom -34 (raw px); anchors x 0.02..0.56.
- grid sep: 6*rs h, 4*rs v.
- item card min 470x76 raw; inner sep 12 raw; badge 54x54 raw; glyph 26 raw; name 16*rs; price 13*rs; tier label 12*rs; owned 12*rs.
- detail: anchor 0.60..0.98, top 110, bottom -34; badge 76x76 raw glyph 36; tier 13*rs; name 24*rs; cost 16*rs; synth 11*rs; diff 14*rs; attrs 13*rs; passive 13*rs; buy button 250x36 raw font 14*rs; price label 12*rs; sell button; total stats 12*rs/15*rs headings.
- owned strip: anchors 0.02..0.98, top 1 offset -30..0; sep 4*rs; buttons 100x28 raw, font 14*rs.

Since all-draw, I need replicating with draw_rect / draw_style_box / draw_string.

Host's grid card heights: 76 raw, rows: GridContainer with 2 columns, cards expand horizontal. Wrap helper:
```
func _wrap(txt: String, max_w: float, sz: float) -> Array:
    var out := []
    var cur := ""
    var cur_w := 0.0
    for i in range(txt.length()):
        var ch := txt[i]
        var w := _f.get_string_size(ch, HORIZONTAL_ALIGNMENT_LEFT, -1, sz).x
        if cur_w + w > max_w and cur != "":
            out.append(cur); cur = ch; cur_w = w
        else:
            cur += ch; cur_w += w
    if cur != "": out.append(cur)
    return out
```

func _draw_plan_line(x0: float, y0: float, max_w: float, rs: float) -> float:
	var plan := _plan()
	var fs := 12.0 * rs
	if plan.is_empty():
		_text(Vector2(x0, y0 + fs), "暂无推荐方案", fs, Color(1, 1, 1, 0.45))
		return y0 + fs * 1.6
	var nxt := _rec
	var x := x0
	var y := y0
	for i in range(plan.size()):
		var id := str(plan[i])
		var nm := str(ItemDatabase.get_item(id).get("name", id))
		var col := Color(1, 1, 1, 0.85)
		if _owned_n(id) > 0:
			col = Color(0.5, 1.0, 0.58)
		elif id == nxt or (nxt == "" and id == _plan_next(plan)):
			col = Color(1.0, 0.88, 0.38)
		var w := _f.get_string_size(nm, HORIZONTAL_ALIGNMENT_LEFT, -1, fs).x
		if x + w > x0 + max_w and x > x0:
			x = x0
			y += fs * 1.4
		_text(Vector2(x, y + fs), nm, fs, col)
		x += w
		if i < plan.size() - 1:
			var arrow := " → "
			var aw := _f.get_string_size(arrow, HORIZONTAL_ALIGNMENT_LEFT, -1, fs).x
			if x + aw > x0 + max_w and x > x0:
				x = x0
				y += fs * 1.4
			_text(Vector2(x, y + fs), arrow, fs, Color(1, 1, 1, 0.3))
			x += aw
	return y + fs * 1.8

Wrap helper:
```
func _wrap(txt: String, max_w: float, sz: float) -> Array:
    var out := []
    var cur := ""
    var cur_w := 0.0
    for i in range(txt.length()):
        var ch := txt[i]
        var w := _f.get_string_size(ch, HORIZONTAL_ALIGNMENT_LEFT, -1, sz).x
        if cur_w + w > max_w and cur != "":
            out.append(cur); cur = ch; cur_w = w
        else:
            cur += ch; cur_w += w
    if cur != "": out.append(cur)
    return out
```

func _gui_input(ev: InputEvent) -> void:
	if ev is InputEventMouseButton:
		var mb := ev as InputEventMouseButton
		if not mb.pressed:
			return
		if mb.button_index == MOUSE_BUTTON_WHEEL_UP or mb.button_index == MOUSE_BUTTON_WHEEL_DOWN:
			if visible:
				_scroll = maxi(_scroll + (-1 if mb.button_index == MOUSE_BUTTON_WHEEL_UP else 1), 0)
				queue_redraw()
				accept_event()
			return
		if mb.button_index != MOUSE_BUTTON_LEFT:
			return
	var press := ev is InputEventMouseButton
	if not press:
		return
	var p: Vector2 = (ev as InputEventMouseButton).position
	var panel := _panel_rect()
	if not panel.has_point(p):
		hide_panel()
		return
	var hit: Dictionary = {}
	for i in range(_hot.size() - 1, -1, -1):
		if (_hot[i]["r"] as Rect2).has_point(p):
			hit = _hot[i]
			break
	if hit.is_empty():
		return
	match str(hit["k"]):
		"close":
			hide_panel()
		"tab":
			var nt := int(hit["a"])
			if nt != _tab:
				_tab = nt
				_scroll = 0
				_sel = ""
				var l := _items_of_tab(_tab)
				if not l.is_empty():
					_sel = str(l[0])
				queue_redraw()
		"item":
			_sel = str(hit["a"])
			queue_redraw()
		"owned":
			var s := int(hit["a"])
			if s >= 0 and s < _equip.size():
				_sel = str(_equip[s])
				queue_redraw()
		"buy":
			var id := str(hit["a"])
			if _afford(id) and (_equip.size() < 6 or _has_component(id)):
				buy(id)
			queue_redraw()
		"sell":
			sell_slot(int(hit["a"]))
			queue_redraw()
		"plannext":
			var pn := str(hit["a"])
			if pn != "" and _gold >= _need_cost(pn):
				buy(pn)
			queue_redraw()

360: # 最深一层缺失的素材件（主机 _find_missing_basic 镜像）
361: func _missing_basic(target_id: String) -> String:
362: 	var target := ItemDatabase.get_item(target_id)
363: 	if target.is_empty() or not target.has("requires"):
364: 		return target_id
365: 	for req_id: String in target.get("requires", []):
366: 		var need := 0
367: 		for r in target["requires"]:
368: 			if str(r) == req_id:
369: 				need += 1
370: 		if _owned_n(req_id) < need:
371: 			return _missing_basic(req_id)
372: 	return target_id
373: 
374: # 下一件（推荐买的第一个：素材齐→合成大件；否则→最底层素材；槽满→补差价合成/升级已有件）
375: func _plan_next(plan: Array) -> String:
376: 	if _equip.size() >= 6:
377: 		# 1. 推荐列表里能补差价合成的（至少持有一件素材）
378: 		for id in plan:
379: 			if _owned_n(id) > 0:
380: 				continue
381: 			for req_id: String in ItemDatabase.get_item(id).get("requires", []):
382: 				if _owned_n(req_id) > 0:
383: 					return id
384: 		# 2. 升级已有低级装（2 阶→合大件 / 1 阶→先合中阶）
385: 		for owned_id in _equip:
386: 			var ot := int(ItemDatabase.get_item(str(owned_id)).get("tier", 1))
387: 			if ot >= 3:
388: 				continue
389: 			if ot == 2:
390: 				for rid in plan:
391: 					if _owned_n(rid) > 0:
392: 						continue
393: 					if str(owned_id) in ItemDatabase.get_item(rid).get("requires", []):
394: 						return rid
395: 			else:
396: 				for rid in plan:
397: 					if _owned_n(rid) > 0:
398: 						continue
399: 					for mid_id: String in ItemDatabase.get_item(rid).get("requires", []):
400: 						if _owned_n(mid_id) > 0:
401: 							continue
402: 						if str(owned_id) in ItemDatabase.get_item(mid_id).get("requires", []):
403: 							return mid_id
404: 		# 3. 兜底第一个未拥有
405: 		for id in plan:
406: 			if _owned_n(id) == 0:
407: 				return id
408: 		return str(plan[0]) if not plan.is_empty() else ""
409: 	# 未满槽：素材齐→合成大件；否则最底层缺失件
410: 	for id in plan:
411: 		if _owned_n(id) > 0:
412: 			continue
413: 		if ItemDatabase.can_build(id, _equip):
414: 			return id
415: 	for id in plan:
416: 		if _owned_n(id) > 0:
417: 			continue
418: 		var miss := _missing_basic(id)
419: 		if miss != "":
420: 			return miss
421: 	return ""
422: 
423: # 现在补多少钱能到手（总价 - 已拥有素材折价）
424: func _need_cost(id: String) -> int:
425: 	var it := ItemDatabase.get_item(id)
426: 	if it.is_empty():
427: 		return 0
428: 	var cost := int(it.get("cost", 0))
429: 	for req_id: String in it.get("requires", []):

431: 		for r in it["requires"]:
432: 			if str(r) == req_id:
433: 				need += 1

Let's test: click owned item first (owned strip) → _sel = owned id, then detail sell hot exists; click sell; check no error; click buy on an affordable selected card; then check plannext click. func click(p, pos: Vector2) -> void:
	var ev := InputEventMouseButton.new()
	ev.button_index = MOUSE_BUTTON_LEFT
	ev.pressed = true
	ev.position = pos
	p._gui_input(ev)

func find(p, kind: String, a=null) -> Rect2:
	for h in p._hot:
		if h["k"] == kind and (a == null or h["a"] == a):
			return h["r"]
	return Rect2()

func _initialize() -> void:
	await process_frame
	var vp := SubViewport.new()
	vp.size = Vector2i(2400, 1400)
	vp.render_target_update_mode = SubViewport.UPDATE_ALWAYS
	root.add_child(vp)
	var p = load("res://scripts/net/NetShopPanel.gd").new()
	vp.add_child(p)
	p.visible = true
	p.feed({"gold": 5000, "name": "吕布", "equip": ["battle_axe", "resist_boots"], "rec": "sage_power"})
	await process_frame
	await process_frame
	print("sel=", p._sel, " buy=", find(p, "buy"), " sell=", find(p, "sell"), " plan=", find(p, "plannext"))
	# 点已拥有条第 0 件 -> 选中 battle_axe，详情应出现「再买一件」+「出售」
	click(p, find(p, "owned", 0).get_center())
	await process_frame
	print("owned click sel=", p._sel, " buy=", find(p, "buy") != Rect2(), " sell=", find(p, "sell") != Rect2())
	# 出售
	var sr := find(p, "sell")
	print("sell rect=", sr)
	click(p, sr.get_center())
	await process_frame
	print("sell click ok")
	# 点一张非拥有卡（第一张）后购买
	var c := find(p, "item")
	click(p, c.get_center())
	await process_frame
	var br := find(p, "buy")
	print("card sel=", p._sel, " buy_rect=", br, " enabled_in_hot=", br != Rect2())
	click(p, br.get_center())
	await process_frame
	print("buy click ok")
	var pr := find(p, "plannext")
	print("plannext=", pr)
	click(p, pr.get_center())
	await process_frame
	print("plan click ok")
	# 滚轮
	var wheel := InputEventMouseButton.new()
	wheel.button_index = MOUSE_BUTTON_WHEEL_DOWN
	wheel.pressed = true
	wheel.position = c.get_center()
	var before: int = p._scroll
	p._gui_input(wheel)
	print("scroll ", before, " -> ", p._scroll)
	quit()

All interactions work. Note: after selecting owned battle_axe and clicking sell, it calls NetSession.send_command; no error. Good.

One thing: When owned item selected, `buy` hot is false while sell true. Why buy false? Condition: `_equip.size() < 6 or _has_component` — equip size 2 <6 true; `_gold >= actual` true; so enabled should be true and hot added. But find(p,"buy") returned false... Because the hot for "buy" was found earlier as `Rect2()`? Wait in probe, `find(p,"buy") != Rect2()` printed false. Hmm! Why? Let's think: after clicking owned item (battle_axe), detail content y differs and buy button should exist.

Maybe because when selecting battle_axe, it's owned; can_more = not owned(tier 3? battle_axe tier 3?) → tier of battle_axe? Let me check: battle_axe probably tier 3 → owned and tier>=3 → can_more false → shows "已拥有 (终极大件)" no buy hot. That explains: battle_axe is tier 3. Fine, correct host behavior.

So sell appeared. ✓.

Another check: for a tier-3 owned item, host shows disabled "已拥有 (终极大件)" and sell. ✓.

Now: In `_draw_detail`, when can_more false, host also does not show 花费 label. ✓.

All good.

Now polish considerations:
1. The selected card in grid doesn't scroll into view if owned item selected from bottom strip; fine.
2. When switching tab, `_scroll=0` and `_sel` first item. ✓.
3. When `_draw` runs with `_sel` empty and list empty (impossible) fine.

Now, question: Should clicking an item card directly buy (original behavior)? I decided select. The Lead's task says "行为兼容" — potential issue. Let me re-read task: "保持现有公开 API 不变：... 方法 feed(o)、toggle()、hide_panel()、buy(id)、sell_slot(slot)、quick_buy()、_draw()、_gui_input/_unhandled_input 行为兼容". "行为兼容" likely means the input still works (O/B/Esc, close, buy/sell via clicks). Our new interaction still supports purchase/sale via detail buttons; but a user clicking a card expecting buy gets selection. Hmm. Is there a way to support both safely? Could make a single click on a card both select AND, if the card was already selected before this click, buy/sell. First click selects (detail preview), second click executes. That's a common pattern (double-tap-ish) and preserves direct-action capability. But might confuse.

Alternatively add a small "购买" hit on the card itself? Host doesn't.

I think host-faithful select-then-buy is right, and I'll clearly state the interaction change in the completion message. The Lead can decide.

Hmm wait — actually let me reconsider. The user complaint: "联机版和单机版的商店面板不太一样". They want visual alignment. If we change interaction to two-tap, net players may find the shop slower but identical to single-player. That's the goal.

Now, one more alignment issue: Host shop's left grid item card click selects, and the grid auto-selects the first item on open. We do. ✓.

Now, are there other host shop visual elements we missed?
- Host card `hover` style: we don't implement hover highlighting (no mouse tracking). On desktop, hover feedback missing. Could add hover via `_gui_input` mouse motion: track `_hover: String` and draw hovered card with selected style. Host hover uses `_item_card_style(tier, true)` — same as selected. Adding hover requires mouse motion events, and queue_redraw on move. That's extra but improves parity. The task doesn't demand hover. Skip (mobile-first).

- Host tabs hover = same as normal selected state; minor.

tools.name: pwsh
tools.description: Execute a PowerShell command (`pwsh -Command`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh pwsh process; pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Paths use native Windows form (`C:\...`); read environment variables with `$env:NAME`. Managed `$env:DSH_*` variables expose current harness environment facts. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. On Windows a force-killed command settles as `[exit code: 1]` without a signal marker — treat it as an interruption, not a command failure. Provide `description` before `command` in the arguments. Before any delete or move, verify that the resolved absolute target path is the intended one; never run it against a computed path you have not checked. Do not assign to automatic variables such as `$HOME`; variable names are case-insensitive, so `$home` is the same read-only variable. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]`, a policy denial: do not retry another way. Under the Windows sandbox, read-only pwsh runs in PowerShell ConstrainedLanguage mode, while workspace-write stays in FullLanguage unless host policy says otherwise. In read-only, prefer cmdlets and core types (`[string]`, `[datetime]`, `[regex]`, `[guid]`); .NET static calls (`[System.IO.*]::`, `[math]::`), `Add-Type`, COM objects, and reflection fail with "only core types" errors. `-f` formatting, property access, and core cmdlets work. In both confined modes, programs cannot open named pipes, so a command that captures another program's output through piped stdio (Node.js `child_process.spawn`/`exec` with the default `stdio: 'pipe'`) fails with EPERM, while `stdio: 'inherit'` and `stdio: 'ignore'` spawns work and PowerShell's own pipelines are unaffected. That EPERM is the documented boundary: do not retry the command another way — escalate the exact command once or restructure it to avoid capturing output.

tools.name: workflow
tools.description:
Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. A stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) end the whole script instead of producing `null`. The script has no filesystem, network, timer, or Node.js APIs; the agents do the work.

script.description: The plain JavaScript body, not TypeScript and without an `export const meta` statement; top-level await is allowed. End with `return <value>`; the JSON-serializable value is this tool's result.

`bs` is Array of `[text:String, Color]`. In RPC, Color is serializable (Variant). Good.

Text: `"  攻击力: +120"` — two leading spaces, "+" already. We draw `text` as-is at detail x (no extra "  " prefix) with color.

Now, colors arriving over RPC: Color objects preserved. But client snapshot may be a Dictionary from RPC; entries are Arrays [String, Color]. Fine.

Implement:
- `var _bs: Array = []` (private) in NetShopPanel.
- feed: `var b = o.get("bs", []); _bs = (b.duplicate() if b is Array else [])`.
- In `_draw_detail` total bonus section: if `_bs` non-empty, draw each row:
  ```
  for row in _bs:
      if y > dby - 24: break
      var txt := str(row[0]) if row is Array and row.size() > 0 else ""
      var col := Color.LIGHT_GREEN
      if row is Array and row.size() > 1:
          var cv = row[1]
          if cv is Color: col = cv
      _text(Vector2(dx, y), txt, fs_tot, col)
      y += fs_tot * 1.35 + 2.0
  ```
  Host's text includes two leading spaces; drawing at dx reproduces indent. Do NOT add "+".
- Else fallback existing `_bonus_totals` loop.

Task says "`bs` 为空时回退到现有近似实现". Note `bs` empty could also legitimately mean no bonuses (hero with no equipment). Host displays nothing in that case; fallback with `_equip` empty also displays nothing. If equip has items but bs empty (e.g., old host), fallback approximate. Good.

Now tab 辅助: host `_shop_categories()` includes "辅助": roam same list as 游走. Task: "先 grep 确认其装备 ID 表，全部加入". We have roam list already. Add `"辅助": [same 12 ids]` to CATS, add `"辅助"` to `_tab_labels`, and `_cat_style` already has "辅助": ["助", Color(0.95,0.86,0.3)].

Task says "8 个 tab 在 2000 宽抽屉里排布不溢出，必要时略微压缩间距但保持 96×42 基准". 0.5px is negligible; but on wider screens rs grows → overflow beyond grid into detail area. Since host does the same, but task explicitly asks to prevent overflow. We can compress gap slightly: use gap = 5.5*rs? At 1.35: 8*129.6+7*7.425=1036.8+51.975=1088.8 → end 1315.8 < 1320. Better. But at rs=1.6875 (3000 wide virtual): 8*162=1296 + 7*9.28=65 = 1361 + x0 33.75 → 1394.75 relative; grid right = 1120 → still overflow horizontally into detail zone (x>1120), but vertical overlap with detail only when th > 65 → rs>1.548. Maybe they mean don't overflow the left grid column (x<1120) before detail. Hmm, at 2400 canvas, 8 tabs end 1320 which is past grid right 1120 and into detail column x 1200.. but vertically tabs end 101.7 and detail starts 110 → no overlap at rs=1.35, so no visual collision. On wider screens, detail starts at 110 too and tabs get taller → overlap; host same. To be safe per task, slightly compress gap to 5*rs and maybe reduce tab width? They said keep 96×42 base. Use gap 5*rs → at 1.35 total = 1036.8+47.25=1084 → end 1311; at 1.6875: 1296+7*8.44=1355.1 + 33.75 = 1388.9 → relative start 33.75, end 1388.9; drawer width 2000, fits; still past 1120. tools.name: pwsh
tools.description: Execute a PowerShell command (`pwsh -Command`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh pwsh process; pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Paths use native Windows form (`C:\...`); read environment variables with `$env:NAME`. Managed `$env:DSH_*` variables expose current harness environment facts. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. On Windows a force-killed command settles as `[exit code: 1]` without a signal marker — treat it as an interruption, not a command failure. Provide `description` before `command` in the arguments. Before any delete or move, verify that the resolved absolute target path is the intended one; never run it against a computed path you have not checked. Do not assign to automatic variables such as `$HOME`; variable names are case-insensitive, so `$home` is the same read-only variable. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]`, a policy denial: do not retry another way. Under the Windows sandbox, read-only pwsh runs in PowerShell ConstrainedLanguage mode, while workspace-write stays in FullLanguage unless host policy says otherwise. In read-only, prefer cmdlets and core types (`[string]`, `[datetime]`, `[regex]`, `[guid]`); .NET static calls (`[System.IO.*]::`, `[math]::`), `Add-Type`, COM objects, and reflection fail with "only core types" errors. `-f` formatting, property access, and core cmdlets work. In both confined modes, programs cannot open named pipes, so a command that captures another program's output through piped stdio (Node.js `child_process.spawn`/`exec` with the default `stdio: 'pipe'`) fails with EPERM, while `stdio: 'inherit'` and `stdio: 'ignore'` spawns work and PowerShell's own pipelines are unaffected. That EPERM is the documented boundary: do not retry the command another way — escalate the exact command once or restructure it to avoid capturing output.

tools.name: workflow
tools.description:
Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. A stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) end the whole script instead of producing `null`. The script has no filesystem, network, timer, or Node.js APIs; the agents do the work.

content.text: Team message from lead:

新任务（HonorKing 工作区 C:\Users\18749\Documents\honor-king，Godot 4.7.2）：UI 打磨 4 项，**你负责联机侧**。用户原话：「右上角金币和装备推荐购买的太小了，导致很难点到；可购买推荐装备时该装备图标四周应该有一圈发光拖尾旋转（技能的加号也需要实现这样的效果）；全局英雄面板在手机端看字太小了；删除英雄头像上方英雄的名字和等级」。

【写作用域】只改 `scripts/net/NetClientBattle.gd`（HUD 内金币/推荐位/环形头像绘制区）、`scripts/net/NetRecommendBar.gd`、`scripts/net/NetRosterPanel.gd`，必要时 `scripts/net/NetTouchPad.gd`（技能键“+”升级标记）。**不要改** `scripts/ui/*`（单机侧由别人并行做）、`scripts/core/*`、`scripts/net/NetLobby.gd`、`NetSession.gd`、`NetShopPanel.gd`。特别注意：NetClientBattle 里属性面板/输入/FX 区段最近刚改过，改动只限 HUD 绘制与推荐带相关函数。

【4 项需求（联机侧，与单机视觉对齐）】
1) **右上角金币与推荐装备购买区域放大、提高可点性**：`NetRecommendBar.gd`（右侧推荐带，含装备卡 + “+” 快速购买）整体放大：装备图标、名称/价格字号、“+”按钮点击区（目标 ≥ 96×96）；`NetClientBattle` HUD 里若有金币显示（grep `gold`/`_format_gold`/顶带绘制）字号/高度同比放大。保证不与小地图/属性面板/技能区重叠（属性面板默认折叠在左侧，小地图在左上）。
2) **可购买推荐装备时：图标四周一圈发光拖尾旋转**：在 `NetRecommendBar` 的装备卡 `_draw` 里加旋转光环拖尾（2~3 段渐变弧 + 尾端淡出，暖金色发光），`_process(delta)` 推进相位；仅在“金币足够可购买”状态绘制（grep 现有 `_rec_show`/`maxed`/金币比较逻辑）。**技能键的“+”升级标记同样加旋转发光**：`NetTouchPad.gd` 里技能按钮的 `+` 升级标记（或 NetClientBattle HUD 技能栏绘制处）加同款旋转光环。
3) **全局英雄面板（联机 C/T 面板 = NetRosterPanel）手机端字号放大**：面板内文字字号整体上调约 20~30%（英雄名/职责/KDA/装备/标题），同步放大行高列宽避免挤压；2400×1400 下不重叠溢出。
4) **删除英雄头像上方的英雄名字与等级**：联机侧英雄头像（NetClientBattle HUD 顶部环形头像带 / NetRosterPanel 面板内头像上方）上方绘制的英雄名 + 等级文字去掉；头像与其余信息保留，别留空白/错位。

【规范】中文一行注释；最小 diff；不改数值平衡；不 commit；不弹通知（Lead 统一发）；临时探针 `_probe_*` 用完删除（含 .import/.uid），最终 `git status --porcelain` 不得有你的 `_probe` 残留。

【验证】
- `D:\Downloads\06_游戏与Flash资源\Godot_v4.7.2-stable_win64.exe\Godot_v4.7.2-stable_win64_console.exe --headless --path . --editor --quit` → exit 0，无 SCRIPT ERROR/Parse Error。
- 冒烟：`--headless --path . scenes/net_client.tscn --quit-after 200` → exit 0 无 SCRIPT ERROR。
- 量化证据（必须）：改造前后推荐带卡片尺寸/“+”点击区尺寸/字号对比；光环仅在可购买状态绘制的分支证据；NetRosterPanel 字号新旧值。
- 视觉验证（建议）：窗口化实例化 `net_client.tscn`（无会话时可只调用 `NetRecommendBar`/`NetRosterPanel` 的绘制或直接 `add_child` 后强制 `_draw`），截图到 `screenshots/` 并给出路径。

【交付】send_message 给 lead：一句话结论；改动 `路径:行号` + 一句说明；验证命令/exit code/新旧数值；未做项与原因。不要贴大段代码。

sandbox_permissions.description: The narrowest wider sandbox mode for a one-shot retry of the exact operation the sandbox just denied; the retry asks the user for approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact file operation needs the wider access. Use the language of the user’s current request.

tools.name: exit_plan_mode
tools.description: Use only in plan mode. Present your plan for the user's review and, on approval, leave plan mode. The user may approve (carry out the plan from your next step) or keep planning — their feedback comes back in the tool result; revise and present again.

plan.description: The complete plan, as markdown, starting with a # heading that names it.

tools.name: glob
tools.description: Find files, not directories, whose paths match a glob pattern, including hidden and ignored files. Returns up to 100 paths in modification-time order; a larger result keeps the first paths and reports where the complete list was saved.

pattern.description: Glob pattern to match file paths against (e.g. "**/*.ts", "src/**/*.test.js"). A pattern with no "/" matches the basename at any depth, so "*" and "*.ts" both search the whole tree; include a separator to anchor the depth.

path.description: Directory to search in. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

tools.name: grep

include.description: One glob filter for which files to search (e.g. "*.ts", "*.{js,jsx}"). Not a list; negation is not supported.

timeout_ms.description: Max wait in milliseconds with wait: true. Defaults to and is capped by configuration.

tools.name: load_workspace_dependencies
tools.description: Get absolute paths to bundled Python and library directories, plus bundled Python distribution versions. Node.js and pnpm paths are included when the payload provides them. Python includes numpy, pandas, python-docx, python-pptx, openpyxl, Pillow, lxml, and XlsxWriter. Use these libraries for Office files unless the user or workspace instructions select another environment. When Node.js and pnpm paths are returned, run pnpm with that Node executable and pnpm script path. This does not change PATH or package-manager settings.

tools.name: present
tools.description: Declare existing files as final deliverables for the user. Use it when the user needs a separate file, especially Office documents, spreadsheets, and slide decks; prefer your final response when that suffices. The user opens the current files; their contents are not copied.

files.description: Usually the 1-2 most important deliverables; at most 4 per call.

path.description: Path of an existing regular file. Relative paths use the Session working directory.

description.description: Brief description for the user.

tools.name: pwsh
tools.description: Execute a PowerShell command (`pwsh -Command`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh pwsh process; pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Paths use native Windows form (`C:\...`); read environment variables with `$env:NAME`. Managed `$env:DSH_*` variables expose current harness environment facts. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. On Windows a force-killed command settles as `[exit code: 1]` without a signal marker — treat it as an interruption, not a command failure. Provide `description` before `command` in the arguments. Before any delete or move, verify that the resolved absolute target path is the intended one; never run it against a computed path you have not checked. Do not assign to automatic variables such as `$HOME`; variable names are case-insensitive, so `$home` is the same read-only variable. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]`, a policy denial: do not retry another way. Under the Windows sandbox, read-only pwsh runs in PowerShell ConstrainedLanguage mode, while workspace-write stays in FullLanguage unless host policy says otherwise. In read-only, prefer cmdlets and core types (`[string]`, `[datetime]`, `[regex]`, `[guid]`); .NET static calls (`[System.IO.*]::`, `[math]::`), `Add-Type`, COM objects, and reflection fail with "only core types" errors. `-f` formatting, property access, and core cmdlets work. In both confined modes, programs cannot open named pipes, so a command that captures another program's output through piped stdio (Node.js `child_process.spawn`/`exec` with the default `stdio: 'pipe'`) fails with EPERM, while `stdio: 'inherit'` and `stdio: 'ignore'` spawns work and PowerShell's own pipelines are unaffected. That EPERM is the documented boundary: do not retry the command another way — escalate the exact command once or restructure it to avoid capturing output.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice, 5-10 words (shown in the UI). Examples: "ls" → "List files in current directory"; "git status" → "Show working tree status"; "Get-Process" → "List running processes".

timeoutMs.description: Timeout in milliseconds. The executor applies its configured default and cap; on expiry the command moves to the background as a job instead of being killed.

workdir.description: Working directory for this command. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path is resolved against it.

run_in_background.description: Run in the background and return a job id immediately (collect with job_output, stop with job_kill). No timeout applies.

sandbox_permissions.description: The narrowest wider sandbox mode for a one-shot retry of the exact command the sandbox just denied; the retry asks the user for approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact command needs the wider access. Use the language of the user’s current request.

offset.description: 1-based first line to return. Defaults to 1.

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to return. Defaults to 2000.

tools.name: read_image
tools.description: Read a PNG/JPEG/WebP/GIF file and return the image itself. Large images are downscaled automatically; do not install image libraries or create thumbnails to inspect an image.

file_path.description: Path to the image file, resolved by the filesystem backend.

tools.name: schedule_create
tools.description: Create a reminder in the current session that delivers prompt when it becomes due. Supply exactly one timing parameter: after_seconds, at, every_seconds, daily, weekly, or cron. Local times that do not exist in the zone are skipped; repeated local times fire once, at the earlier instant. After downtime, a recurring reminder delivers only its latest missed occurrence. Delivery can repeat after a crash.

prompt.description: Reminder content to present when the target becomes due.

title.description: Concise task name in the user's language, at most 120 characters. Name only the core action and subject; keep essential target identifiers such as PR numbers and branch names. Do not include execution frequency (e.g. daily, hourly), scheduled dates/times, time zones, task status, or configuration and execution details (e.g. read-only mode, profile-tag filters), even when embedded in the requested or existing title. Do not append parenthetical notes. Put scheduling information in the timing parameters and execution instructions in prompt.

every_seconds.description: Fixed-rate interval in whole seconds, at least 60, aligned to the creation time; changing it with schedule_update re-aligns it to the save time.

daily.description: Every day at a local time.

time.description: HH:mm:ss with optional 1-3 fractional digits, for example 23:00:00.

time_zone.description: UTC or IANA Area/Location, for example Asia/Shanghai.

weekly.description: On the given weekdays at a local time.

time.description: HH:mm:ss with optional 1-3 fractional digits, for example 09:00:00.

tools.name: workflow
tools.description:
Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. A stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) end the whole script instead of producing `null`. The script has no filesystem, network, timer, or Node.js APIs; the agents do the work.

script.description: The plain JavaScript body, not TypeScript and without an `export const meta` statement; top-level await is allowed. End with `return <value>`; the JSON-serializable value is this tool's result.

model.description: Optional model override this phase is expected to use.

args.description: Optional JSON input exposed to the script as the `args` global (wrap a bare list as a field, e.g. {"files": [...]}).

run_in_background.description: Run as a background job: return a job id immediately instead of waiting; the return value arrives with the completion notice.
